content.title: Regimens and treatment durations with non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants (NOACs)
content.recommendation_summary: All patients with pulmonary embolism (PE) should receive anticoagulant therapy for at least 3 months. After this period, decision on extended anticoagulation should balance risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) versus bleeding risk; NOACs have generally lower bleeding rates than VKAs but are not without risk.
content.trial_population: In NOAC extended-treatment trials, patients with PE comprised approximately one-third of the study populations; the remaining two-thirds had proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) without clinically overt PE.

dabigatran.efficacy: Dabigatran was non-inferior to warfarin for prevention of confirmed recurrent symptomatic VTE or VTE-related death, and more effective than placebo for prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE or unexplained death.
dabigatran.safety: Rate of major bleeding with dabigatran was 0.9% versus 1.8% with warfarin (reported HR 0.52, 95% CI approximately 0.27–1.02).
dabigatran.context: Two studies compared dabigatran with warfarin or placebo in extended treatment of VTE.

dose_regimens: 20 mg or 10 mg o.d. compared with aspirin 100 mg o.d.
rivaroxaban.efficacy: Rivaroxaban 20 mg o.d. reduced recurrent VTE (reported ~48% relative reduction versus comparator). Rivaroxaban at 20 or 10 mg o.d. reduced symptomatic recurrent fatal or non-fatal VTE versus aspirin in the aspirin-comparison study.
rivaroxaban.safety: Reported incidence of major or clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding with rivaroxaban in one comparison was 6.0% versus 1.2% with placebo. No significant differences in rates of major or CRNM bleeding were shown between rivaroxaban doses and aspirin in the aspirin comparison.
rivaroxaban.study_size_note: One rivaroxaban versus aspirin study included 3,365 patients.
rivaroxaban.context: Rivaroxaban was tested versus placebo/aspirin in extended-treatment trials after 6–12 months of initial anticoagulation for a first VTE event.

apixaban.efficacy: Both doses of apixaban reduced incidence of symptomatic recurrent VTE or death from any cause compared with placebo.
apixaban.safety: No safety concerns reported in the referenced extended-treatment studies.
apixaban.context: Patients with VTE were randomized to two apixaban doses or placebo after 6–12 months of initial anticoagulation.

content.general_safety_and_exclusions: Phase III extended-treatment trials reported major bleeding rates up to ~1% (example: dabigatran) and CRNM bleeding up to ~6% in some settings. Patients judged to be at high bleeding risk by investigators (based on history and laboratory results) were excluded from the extension studies.
content.notes: Text refers generically to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) as comparator class. Supplementary Data tables are cited for detailed trial summaries.
